News.title: Is Zack Polanski wrong for wanting to ban horse racing?  VOTE NOW
News.content:
POLL OF THE DAY Is Zack Polanski wrong for wanting to ban horse racing? VOTE NOW

ZACK Polanski has called for horse racing to be banned as millions gear up for the Grand National at Liverpool’s Aintree.

The Green leader has galloped into a row by claiming the sport was animal cruelty and has even gone as far as saying all equestrian events should be banned from the Olympics.



Money-spinning meetings such as those at Cheltenham and Royal Ascot would be axed if the Greens reach No 10.



It prompted Reform UK’s leader Nigel Farage to blast his views as “cranky nonsense” and labelled the idea as “utterly absurd”.

The Green leader’s stance on banning horse racing goes further than his party’s official policy which calls for a ban on using whips in the sport.

Mr Polanski, born David Paulden, even refuses to wear clothing that shows horse riding because of his vegan beliefs.

Racing is the UK’s most popular spectator sport after football. It pumps £4.1billion a year into the UK economy and supports more than 85,000 jobs, according to the British Horseracing Authority.



The three-day Grand National Festival at Aintree is worth £60million to the Liverpool economy alone.

So, what do you think? Is Zack Polanski wrong for wanting to ban horse racing? Have your say in our exclusive poll.

News.title: Teen boy, 14, seriously injured by two dogs in horror attack after they escaped from house in UK village
News.content:
MAUL TERROR Teen boy, 14, seriously injured by two dogs in horror attack after they escaped from house in UK village

A TEEN boy has been seriously injured by two dogs after they escaped from a house in a UK village.

Emergency services raced to the scene in Potterne, Wiltshire last night after the 14-year-old was mauled in a horror attack.



The shocking incident happened at around 9.30pm on Thursday after the pets escaped a nearby property, reports Wiltshire 999s.

Paramedics rushed the teen boy to hospital as armed cops fought to bring the animals under control.



Wiltshire Police seized both dogs as they were carted off in the back of a van and taken to secure kennels.

Their owner is reportedly due to be interviewed under caution with the breed of the dogs yet to be confirmed.

Devizes Neighbourhood Inspector Simon Garrett said: “We appreciate how horrendous and distressing this incident must have been for the victim, his family and those who witnessed it and we are taking it very seriously.

“The two dogs involved have been seized and taken to secure kennels and their owner has been identified.

“Enquiries are ongoing to understand the full circumstances of the incident.”

Anyone with information on the attack is urged to get in touch with the police.

News.title: Traumatised girl, 10, gives birth to sick rapist stepfather’s baby after twisted mum ‘tried to hide pregnancy’
News.content:
PAEDO FATHER Traumatised girl, 10, gives birth to sick rapist stepfather’s baby after twisted mum ‘tried to hide pregnancy’

A TRAUMATISED ten-year-old girl gave birth to her rapist stepdad’s baby after falling pregnant to the monster – and the child’s twisted mother tried to protect him.

A 23-year-old man and 30-year-old woman were arrested in Brazil after the shocking case came to light.





The vile predator is under investigation for the repeated rape of his two stepdaughters, aged eight and ten, while the mother was cuffed for trying to conceal his crimes.

Cops swooped in on the couple, who have not been named, after they fled the city of Itacoatiara in a bid to hide the girl’s pregnancy.

The horrific abuse only came to light when the ten-year-old went into labour and gave birth on April 3.

Hospital staff alerted police due to the girl’s young age, and the mother subsequently gave a contradicting statement with the aim of protecting her partner.



Police spokesperson Bruno Rafael said: “We found that the couple left Itacoatiara, along with the children, motivated by the physical changes caused by the pregnancy in the 10-year-old child’s body.”

He added: “Tests confirmed that both sisters were victims of statutory rape.

“The justice system acted quickly, preventive detention was ordered, and the mother lost custody of her daughters.

“She was arrested at the hospital, and the stepfather was captured in the city centre.”



After the rescue, the victims underwent specialised listening sessions and confirmed that the rapes were committed by their stepfather.

They will be placed under the care of their aunt.

The two suspects will remain in custody while judicial proceedings continue.

It comes after a similarly tragic case when an 11-year-old girl gave birth to her stepfather’s child in Oklahoma last August.

Dustin Walker, 34, was arrested after DNA testing revealed the baby had a 99.9 per cent match to him.



The vile predator pleaded guilty to several charges including sexually abusing a child under the age of 12 last month, according to court records.

Walker and the girl’s mum, Cherie, claimed they didn’t know the girl, who hadn’t been to a doctor in a year, was pregnant after the arrest.

Mrs Walker was charged with enabling child sexual abuse, while her husband was charged with sexually abusing the girl.

In a statement, Muskogee County Assistant District Attorney Janet Hutson said: “This is one of the most if not the most serious child sexual abuse and neglect cases I have ever prosecuted.

“This child is traumatised. She’s been through a horrific ordeal. I mean, not only has somebody gotten her pregnant, but she gave birth at home without medical assistance, and this will be her life for the rest of her life.”

She added: “Each of the charges against both defendants are punishable by up to life.”

News.title: ‘Serious failures’ as deadly asbestos is found in 3 more toys after string of ‘shocking’ recalls in UK – see full list
News.content:
CONSUMER watchdogs have slammed “serious failures” as three more children’s toys are recalled over asbestos concerns.

It comes after a number of toys were pulled from shelves across the UK over the toxic ingredient in recent weeks.





Three stretchy toys have been added to the nationwide recall list over concerns that they contained sand contaminated with asbestos.

Batches of the HGL Stretchy Sand Monster Truck, Scrunchems Stretchies Sleepy Dino Toy and HGL Stretchy Sand Pig have all been pulled from shelves, with parents warned to bin them immediately.

The following model and barcodes are included in the recall:

HGL Stretchy Sand Monster Truck – model number: SV21889 and barcode: 5021813218894

Scrunchems Stretchies Sleepy Dino Toy – model number: 38758 and barcode: 5038728153109

HGL Stretchy Sand Pig – model number: SV21795 and barcode: 5021813217954

Speaking on the issue, Sue Davies, Which? Head of Consumer Protection Policy, said: “It is shocking that deadly asbestos is once again being found in children’s toys sold at major retailers.

“This points to serious failures in product safety checks.”

She continued: “Manufacturers and retailers must urgently review their supplier oversight and testing to make sure unsafe products are not reaching stores in the first place.

“The Office for Product Safety and Standards needs to take action and ensure proper checks are being carried out to keep dangerous products off the shelves.



“It should also examine whether toys containing asbestos are being sold on online marketplaces where there is far more limited regulation.”

According to recall notices issued by the Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS), the affected batches could “pose a risk to health” due to possible contamination with a “small quantity” of asbestos.

Asbestos is a banned substance which poses a risk to health even at low levels of exposure, meaning the product does not meet the requirements of the Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011.

The toxic ingredient causes mesothelioma, a cancer which usually starts in the layers of tissue that cover the lungs.

All three toys are distributed by One For Fun Limited and are reported to originate from China, with OPSS advising that additional distributors may be added to the list as more information becomes available.



In a statement, One For Fun chief executive David Mordecai said: “We are aware of recent global reports concerning the presence of trace asbestos in sand used within certain consumer products.

“This has affected many toy companies throughout the world.”

He said the company has “immediately conducted independent testing” across its full range of sand-filled items “as a precautionary measure”.

“While current safety standards (EN71) do not require testing for asbestos, our investigations identified that three of our products contained trace contamination,” he continued.

“These products have been withdrawn from the market.



“We take product safety extremely seriously. As a result, we have discontinued the use of sand as a filler in all current and future products.

“We remain committed to the highest safety standards and will continue to monitor and review our materials and processes accordingly.”

The OPSS outlined the best course of action for anyone in possession of an affected toy, recommending it is kept out of the reach of children and disposed of carefully.

If the sand is still in the packaging, parents are advised to place the item “in a heavy-duty plastic bag, double tape it securely, label it clearly and store in a secure location out of the reach of children”.

And if the sand has been used, parents should “clean up sites where the product was used using wet cloths to avoid generating dust”.



Anyone coming into contact with the product or surfaces it has touched is recommended to wear gloves and a mask, before double bagging them along with the sand and any cloth used.

Children and other people should be kept away from areas where the sand has been used until the area has been cleaned.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Customers are advised to return the product to the place of purchase for redress.

For further information, consumers can contact One For Fun Limited on +44 (0)141 613 2525 or help@oneforfun.com.

News.title: Hunter Biden offers to fight Trump’s sons in CAGE MATCH – as his ‘$17million debt and exile abroad’ is revealed
News.content:
HUNTER Biden has sensationally offered to have a cage fight with Donald Trump’s sons as he looks to continue their father’s feud.

Hunter, 56, said he is “100 per cent in” to have a scrap against Donald Jr and Eric if the money is right after it was claimed the former president’s son is $17million in debt and now lives abroad.





A new Washington court filing claims Joe Biden‘s controversial offspring no longer lives in the US and argues he “cannot afford” to pay outstanding legal bills.

He is currently being sued by his former attorneys at Winston & Strawn after the law firm defended him in his tax and gun crimes cases in the past.

They allege he owes legal fees “substantially in excess of $50,000” – an amount he can’t pay back, according to a new legal filing submitted by his attorney Barry Coburn, uncovered by the Daily Mail.

Just last year, lifelong Democrat Hunter claimed he was in $17million of debt.

An easy money-making move may have now fallen on Hunter’s lap after he declared his interest in a cage fight with long-standing family rivals.

Hunter announced that he has been asked about a potential political showdown more than a decade in the making.

He ⁠said he recently got a call from left-wing social media commentator Andrew ​Callaghan, who told him he wanted to get Eric and Donald Trump Jr to agree to agree to a fight.



Hunter said in a video about the lucrative proposal: “I think he’s trying to organise a cage match, me versus Eric and Don Jr.

“I told him I’d do it, 100% in, if he can pull it off.”

Callaghan was asked about the fight by USA TODAY, to which he replied his comments were originally “in jest”.

But he stated he’s “more than happy to facilitate” if both sides are “willing to engage in mutual combat”.

Echoing the infamous father-son rivalry of Conor Benn and Chris Eubank Jr last year, a fight between the Bidens and Trumps would be a must-see affair for many.



The Biden family are currently undefeated when going toe-to-toe with the Trumps.

In 2020, Joe and Donald faced off to see who would become the president of the United States.

Despite the election result being marred by unsavoury controversy, Joe Biden rose to power beating Trump by 74 Electoral College votes.

Trump quickly branded the 2020 election the “greatest fraud in US history” and continues to claim he was unfairly defeated.

Any sign of foul play has never been proven over the election result.



The two heavyweight political figures were set to do battle at the polls again four years later.

Trump bashed his foe as the pair had their first debate of the run-in before the Democrats pulled Biden from the election over his ill-health concerns.

Vice President Kamala Harris took her long-time friend’s place on the ballot sheet but she was heavily defeated by Trump who strode back into the White House.



Trump has refused to let up on his verbal put-downs of Biden since returning to the Oval Office.

Sleepy Joe, Crooked Joe and Crazy Joe Biden are all among the nicknames the US leader often gives his rival during speeches or Truth Social posts.

The Trump administration even ended Hunter’s Secret Service protection last year.

The president said it was “ridiculous” he still had 18 agents protecting him – all of whom are paid for by the taxpayer.

Biden‘s daughter, Ashley, who has 13 agents for protection, was also “taken off the list”.

News.title: Brits’ top everyday annoyances are queue jumpers, loud chewers and stuck jars, study finds
News.content:
BRITS’ biggest everyday annoyances include queue jumpers, loud chewers and struggling to open jars.

A poll of 2,000 adults revealed the small things that irritate them the most, with forgetting about a cup of tea until it goes cold, stubbing a toe and chipping a nail also on the list.





A further 15 per cent get exasperated by cryptic social media posts, and a huge 43 per cent fume lateness.

It’s not just social behaviours that annoy people – it’s also everyday tasks like hanging up picture frames that end up wonky (11 per cent).

Other day to day activities people find annoying are waiting for a bus or train to arrive only for it to turn up late (35 per cent) and opening tin cans (nine per cent).

When working on tasks like these, nine per cent admitted their tolerance only lasts up to five minutes before they reach the end of their tether.

It also emerged one in four will make just three attempts at a challenging practical job before running out of patience and abandoning it.

Kim McMahon from Chupa Chups, which commissioned the research to mark the launch of its new easier to open wrapper, said: “I’m sure we can all relate to these everyday annoyances, it’s surprising how something seemingly small can have a big impact on our moods.

“Often, it’s things which are out of our control like what other people post on social media, being unable to open a tight lid or loud eaters and it’s easier said than done to control the way we react.

“Vice versa, we probably all do things which annoy others too and this list of pet peeves will have you second guessing.



“It felt natural to tap into this topic for us given the well-known struggles with lollipop packaging and consumers getting openly frustrated on social media.

“Saving a moment or two can really impact your overall day or even week.”

The study also found a quarter of those polled find themselves irritated by minor inconveniences, particularly when they’re already tired (39 per cent), running late (33 per cent) or hungry (21 per cent).

For 31 per cent, public transport leads the way as a hotspot for frustration, with supermarkets and their homes also ranking highly as places they’re likely to be faced with disruptions.

Even tasks like opening food packaging winds up more than a third (35 per cent) and unwrapping lollipops was considered a challenging task by 43 per cent.



It also emerged that while 37 per cent of people blame themselves for everyday irritations, 14 per cent point the finger at their partners.

On the plus side, 52 per cent are likely to seek resolutions to avoid annoyance and save themselves time, and for 17 per cent it’s just about trying something new.

With some of the top hacks including using scissors to cut pizza (20 per cent), wearing gloves to open jars (23 per cent) and microwaving cold tea (24 per cent).

More than four in 10 claimed their family is the most inspiring source for time-slashing methods, along with TV shows (21 per cent), according to the research by OnePoll.

But for 29 per cent, the easiest way to reset after a jarring incident is by taking deep breaths, whereas self-indulgence is the way forward for 19 per cent.



Harry Aikines-Aryeetey, also known as Nitro from Gladiators, took to the streets with Chupa Chups to investigate the nation’s annoyances.

He said: “People know me for strength and speed, but even as a Gladiator, it’s the little things that can test your patience the most.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

”Getting out and about to chat to the public I saw it firsthand; you train for big moments but no one trains for a jar that won’t budge or a lollipop wrapper that just won’t open – it can be humbling.

“But what surprised me most is how universal it all is. We’re all dealing with small frustrations, day in, day out and while we can’t control everything, making even the smallest things easier can genuinely lift your mood and keep your day moving.”

News.title: Ann Summers sex toy is urgently recalled over fears ‘parts will detach during use’
News.content:
BAD VIBRATIONS Ann Summers sex toy is urgently recalled over fears ‘parts will detach during use’

A SEX toy has been urgently recalled after concerns that parts may detach during use.

An Ann Summers vibrator was removed from shelves after a fault with the ‘internal mechanism’, according to the retailer.



Because of this, the UK’s Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) has said the toy presents “a risk of injuries as it is possible for parts to detach during use.



“The product does not meet the requirements of the General Product Safety Regulations 2005.”

The company has urged customers to stop using the Remote Rotating Dildo immediately and to return it in store or by post for free.

The dodgy toy has also been removed from all Ann Summers stores and online retailers.

As a gesture of goodwill, Ann Summers has said customers will receive a full refund and an additional 20% off their next purchase.

The brand said: “Customer safety and product quality are our highest priority”.

But this is not the first toy to cause the erotic retailer some trouble.

The Thrusting Ring Rabbit toy was removed from shelves last year after a similar issue.

Online users have commented thinking the recall was initially a ‘joke’.



One shopper warned others to be careful and to “please check your model babes”.

News.title: Girl, 16, ‘murdered by three teens in street after party’ died from single stab wound to the chest, inquest told
News.content:
KNIFE HORROR Girl, 16, ‘murdered by three teens in street after party’ died from single stab wound to the chest, inquest told

A SCHOOLGIRL died from a single stab wound to the chest after she was allegedly attacked in the street, an inquest heard.

Chloe Watson, 16, was discovered unresponsive after a party in Leeds, West Yorkshire, on March 28.





She was rushed to hospital where sadly she could not be saved and pronounced her dead a short time later.

Kayla Smith, 18, Archie Rycroft, 19, and a 17-year-old boy, who cannot legally be named, have since been charged with murder.

An inquest heard today how Chloe’s heartbroken father Mark Dransfield had to formally identify his daughter.

Area coroner Oliver Longstaff said a post mortem found Chloe died from a stab wound to her chest.

The coroner also said Chloe met a “violent death” as he suspended proceedings until the outcome of the criminal trial.

Chloe’s alleged killers will next appear at Leeds Crown Court for a plea and trial hearing on May 1.

A provisional trial set to last three weeks has been scheduled for November.



Chloe’s distraught mum previously paid tribute to her “beautiful princess”.

She wrote: “I cannot put into words how I feel that you are not here with me.

“You are my life, my world, my best friend and I know that I am yours. I cannot live without you – I need you.

“You are stunning, confident, loyal, honest and my family-oriented princess.

“When you walk into any room it lights up with your bubbly personality.



“There is so much I could say. There’s a big hole in my heart that can never be filled.

“Your two sisters and big brother will always love and miss you to infinity.

“You will always and forever be in our hearts. Love Mum, Connor, Courtney and Cienna.”

Her father’s family also issued a tribute in the wake of the killing describing their “immeasurable” heartache.

It read: “We miss every single thing about her. She was beautiful, full of joy, and had a wonderfully cheeky personality.



“She embraced life with such happiness, and she had her whole future ahead of her.

“Chloe was loved by everyone who knew her, and the absence she leaves behind is immeasurable.

“We will miss her forever, she will never be forgotten.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A GoFundMe has since been set up by Chloe’s cousin Shantelle.

The force is still looking to hear from people who could help with their investigation.

News.title: HMRC allowance renewal key decision 'leaves savers £17,000 better off'
News.content:
HMRC allowance renewal key decision 'leaves savers £17,000 better off'

With the new tax year starting this week, people are being alerted

View 3 Images Timing is important, experts say (Image: Patamaporn Umnahanant via Getty Images)

Financial experts have said that making a key decision when it comes to saving into a tax-free ISA "could boost your investments by thousands of pounds". ISAs are protected from being taxed by HMRC and £20,000 can be put into them each year.

‌



This could be put into a cash ISA that earns straight interest like any savings account, or put into a stocks and shares ISA, which is linked to the stock market. Savers can split their £20,000 across different types of ISA and from next year, 2027, the cash element will change to £12,000, although the overall allowance will remain at £20,000.

‌



New analysis from J.P. Morgan Personal Investing has shone a light on how investing early and regularly in the tax year over the past decade would have boosted UK investors’ portfolios.

‌



It said that investing the average annual ISA contribution - according to HMRC data - of £7,594 each year since 2016/17 into a stocks and shares ISA would be worth £135,600 by the end of the 2025/2026 tax year if the money was drip‑fed monthly into a global markets tracker.

However, if savers had invested the same annual amount as a lump sum at the start of each tax year, over the same 10-year period they would have achieved a portfolio value of £149,400. By contrast, savers would have a smaller portfolio of £132,500 if the lump sum was invested at the end of each tax year - a difference of nearly £17,000.

View 3 Images J.P. Morgan has published new research and advice (Image: CYH via Getty Images)

‌



It said the sums were based on an individual investing in the MSCI All Country World Index (LSE: ACWI) and reinvesting dividends.

Claire Exley, head of financial advice and guidance at J.P. Morgan Personal Investing, said: “The start of the new tax year is an important moment for investors and savers as the annual ISA allowance refreshes. Many will be considering their strategy for contributing money into their tax-free ISA wrapper and deploying any excess savings into the market.

“For investors, historical data shows that investing earlier in the tax year could boost your investments by thousands of pounds over the long-term.

‌



"While past performance isn't a reliable guide for future performance, the 10-year data suggests that investors who stayed invested in global markets for longer were better off compared to those who waited until the final week of the tax year to invest.

"The 12-month gap in contributions can make a significant difference when compounding takes effect and boosts an investment portfolio. While we would never suggest trying to time the market, we do advocate giving your investments time in the market as long-term investing increases the probability of generating profits and allows more time to benefit from tax-free compounding.

View 3 Images ISAs offer tax-free savings (Image: Laurence Berger via Getty Images)

Article continues below

"For those who cannot deploy a lump sum, making monthly contributions into your stocks and shares ISA has the benefit of drip-feeding money into financial markets in a tax-efficient way.

"This approach can help smooth out any periods of volatility as we are currently experiencing in markets and have seen in the past when the pandemic impacted global markets.”

J.P. Morgan stressed that, as with all investing, your capital is at risk. The value of your portfolio can go down as well as up and you may get back less than you invest. Tax rules vary by individual status and may change.

News.title: Gastroenterologist says rule of 'three' can add years to your life
News.content:
Gastroenterologist says rule of 'three' can add years to your life

A doctor has explained a simple rule backed by a study of 59,000 people that could help you live longer through small daily changes

View Image The study looked at more than 59,000 people (Image: Getty)

A doctor has revealed a straightforward rule which he claims could extend people's lives by a year. The simple '5+2 rule' requires just seven minutes and could significantly boost your overall wellbeing.

‌



Dr Will Bulsiewicz is a gastroenterologist who goes by the name Gut Health MD. He boasts a substantial social media following and regularly shares health-related content.

‌



He revealed that a recent study involving 59,000 participants in January 2026 demonstrated that 'small, consistent wins across three areas' could all contribute to increased longevity. He said: "Five minutes of sleep. Two minutes of exercise. One more year of life.

‌



"A study of 59,000 people just proved you don't need a massive lifestyle overhaul to live longer - you need small, consistent wins across three areas."

He added: "We've been told that living longer requires a complete lifestyle overhaul. A new study of 59,000 people says otherwise.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"Researchers tracked 59,078 people using wearable accelerometers - measuring actual sleep, exercise, and diet quality over years of follow-up. Here's what the minimum effective dose looked like:

+5mins/day of sleep

+2min/day of moderate exercise

‌



+1/2 serving of vegetables /day

= 1 additional year of life

+24mins/day of sleep

‌



+4mins/day of exercise

+A meaningful diet upgrade

=4 additional years disease-free (Disease-free = no heart disease, cancer, diabetes, COPD, or dementia)

‌



"People who optimised all three - 7-8 hours sleep, _42 minutes of daily exercise, and a high-quality diet - gained: 9.35 extra years of lifespan and 9.45 extra years of healthspan. Nearly a decade - let that sink in.

"Here's the thing: It's not any single change that matters most. It's the combination. Sleep + movement + food quality working together. Small improvements in all three beat a dramatic improvement in just one.

"This is what I've been shouting from the rooftops! Progress over perfection, you don't need to run a marathon or eat grass. Small changes done consistently yield huge results - years of life.

‌



"Stop waiting for the perfect plan. Start with five more minutes of sleep tonight, a two-minute walk after lunch, and an extra handful of greens on your plate. The science says that's enough to start adding years."

The research

The research itself was entitled 'Minimum combined sleep, physical activity, and nutrition variations associated with lifeSPAN and healthSPAN improvements: a population cohort study'. It was put together by Nicholas A. Koemel, Raaj K. Biswas, Matthew N. Ahmadi, Armando Teixeira-Pinto, Mark Hamer, and Leandro F.M. Rezende.

Its declared objective was: "Sleep, physical activity, and nutrition (SPAN) are key determinants of both life expectancy (lifespan) and disease-free life expectancy (healthspan), yet are often studied in isolation. This study aimed to determine the minimum combined SPAN improvements needed for a longer lifespan and healthspan." The research yielded the findings that Dr Bulsiewicz referenced, before determining: "Modest concurrent improvements in sleep, physical activity, and diet were associated with meaningful gains in lifespan and healthspan."

Article continues below

It added: "This study demonstrates that small, concurrent improvements in sleep, physical activity, and diet quality were associated with clinically meaningful theoretical gains in lifespan and healthspan. These findings inform future trials and public health interventions by highlighting a pragmatic approach to improving population health that involves combined modest behavioural changes."

News.title: 'My heart sank when summoned by King Charles - but then he asked me a surprising question’
News.content:
'My heart sank when summoned by King Charles - but then he asked me a surprising question’

Anne Tennant, Baroness Glenconner, a peeress who wrote a piece about King Charles' Coronation in 2023, thought she was "in trouble" when the message first arrived

View 3 Images Lady Glenconner received a summons from King Charles (Image: Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

A peeress whose heart "sank" when she received a summons from King Charles has revealed how the monarch asked her a surprising four-word question. Anne Tennant, Baroness Glenconner, a 93-year-old peeress and socialite who was selected as one of the maids of honour at the Coronation of the late Queen Elizabeth II, thought she was "in trouble" when the message first arrived.

‌



The moment came after Lady Glenconner wrote about Charles' Coronation in May 2023, having had the privilege of attending both the current monarch’s ceremony and that of her childhood friend, Elizabeth.

‌



Initially, Anne's "heart sank" when she heard that Buckingham Palace wanted to speak to her — she feared the worst — but it ultimately resulted in a dinner invitation from the King.

‌



She told The Mail's Richard Eden: "I got a call from my daughter, Amy. She said, 'Buckingham Palace wants to get in touch with you', so my heart sank because I thought I was in trouble."

View 3 Images Lady Glenconner thought she was "in trouble" when the message first arrived (Image: Getty Images)

Instead, Lady Glenconner was invited to a "one-on-one dinner", during which the monarch put a question to her about the royal occasion. She explained: "He looked at me and said, 'How was it, Anne?' I said, 'Magnificent, sir, but different'," adding that it "had to be".

‌



Just one day after the Coronation on May 7 that year, the Mail published a first-person account by Lady Glenconner, in which she described the royal proceedings.

In one segment, she wrote: "The historical heart of the service, the anointing of the new monarch with holy oil, was the same solemn ritual it has always been.

"The King was divested of his robes and wore just a simple shift for this private and sacred moment, which took place, away from the public gaze and TV cameras, behind screens."

‌



Lady Glenconner, who also penned the memoirs Lady in Waiting and Whatever Next?, concluded her piece by detailing how guests "waved like mad" as the new King and Queen made their exit.

View 3 Images Lady Glenconner was invited to a "one-on-one dinner" with Charles (Image: Getty Images)

She wrote: "We all waved like mad as our dear new King and Queen left in their very uncomfortable gold coach — but I had to wait until I got home to sit down and enjoy a stiff vodka and tonic."

Article continues below

In other news, King Charles is expected to lead tributes marking what would have been his mother's 100th birthday on April 21. As part of the commemorations, the King will address the nation and celebrate her life.

Charles and Camilla will also host a reception at the palace for representatives from organisations and charities with links to the late Queen, with insiders claiming that the King's written tribute will highlight Elizabeth's achievements.

It is also expected to include a video montage featuring clips from the late Queen's Auxiliary Territorial Service service during World War II, alongside footage from her tours and engagements.

News.title: The jaw-dropping speed Artemis II will splash down to Earth is hard to fathom
News.content:
The jaw-dropping speed Artemis II will splash down to Earth is hard to fathom

The Orion capsule carrying the four Artemis II astronauts will reach incredible speeds and temperatures as it splashes down into the Pacific Ocean. Here's everything you need to know

View Image A visualisation of the Artemis I spacecraft re-entering Earth's atmosphere as Artemis II prepares to splash down in the Pacific Ocean (Image: NASA)

Nasa's historic Artemis II mission will come to an end today, Friday, as the four astronauts crash back to Earth after travelling further into space than any human ever has before. The crew are due to splashdown off the coast of San Diego, California, later today.

‌



And the capsule will reach astonishing speeds as it re-enters Earth's atmosphere. Speaking at a press conference yesterday, Thursday, Nasa associate administrator Amit Kshatriya explained what will happen as the crew of three Americans and one Canadian return to Earth.

‌



"Tomorrow the Orion spacecraft will enter the Earth's atmosphere at approximately 25,000mph," he said. "That heat shield, the thermal protection system, which is built by American hands and American factories from materials designed to withstand temperatures that approach the surface of the Sun, will bear the full force of that re-entry.

‌



"Every system that we've demonstrated over the past nine days - life support, navigation, propulsion, communications, all of it - depends on the final minutes of flight. We have high confidence in the system, in the heat shield, in the parachutes, in the recovery systems we put together.

"The engineering supports it, the Artemis I flight data supports it, all of our ground test supports it, our analysis supports it, and tomorrow the crew is going to put their lives behind that confidence."

He added there was "no question" the ground team was anxious, but added he had full confidence all the necessary preparations had been made. "It's impossible to say you don't have irrational fears left, right? But I would tell you I don't have any rational fears about what's going to happen."

‌



Lakiesha Hawkins, Nasa’s acting deputy associate administrator for exploration systems development, said: “When a mission goes well, it can look like flying to the Moon is easy. It certainly is not.

“We can’t forget that this is a test flight, and are taking everything that we’re learning forward to support the next mission. This has been a good mission so far, and we’re nearing the end, having retired a significant number of risks over recent days, but the team remains focused, and we’re making sure that we don’t take our eye off the ball.

“Countless hours of people working together behind the scenes have been preparing for these moments, and people are still giving their all to ensure mission success. We continue to improve, to make our ultimate goals of going to the lunar surface, building the moon base and eventually sending the first humans to Mars, a reality.”

‌



The last time Nasa sent astronauts to the Moon was as part of the Apollo 17 mission in 1972. The agency is seeking to return a crew to the lunar surface by 2028, before China does in about 2030.

What will happen as Artemis II mission returns to Earth?

The shockwave created as the the capsule re-enters the Earth's atmosphere will see the air surrounding the craft reach temperatures of 10,000 degrees or higher. The heat shield is just a few inches thick and is designed to burn away, transferring heat away from the capsule.

Article continues below

Communications with mission control will be disrupted as the capsule falls 400,000 feet, with the crew experiencing 3.9Gs, nearly four times normal gravity. Two sets of parachutes will open when it gets closer to landing, with the crew due to splash down in the Pacific at 5.07pm local time, or 1.07am on Saturday morning in the UK.

The time between re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere and landing in the Pacific Ocean will be about 13 minutes. Speaking at the press conference, mission flight director Rick Henfling said: “So it’s going to happen pretty quick.”

He added: “It’s very dynamic. So similarly to the launch environment, there’s not a lot of time to react.” The navy’s USS John P Murtha is currently en-route to meet the capsule when it lands. You can watch the landing live here.

News.title: Woman's desperate final hours before she plunged to her death to escape evil husband
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Woman's desperate final hours before she plunged to her death to escape evil husband

WARNING DISTRESSING CONTENT: Kimberley Milne endured 18 months of torment at the hands of her violent and manipluative husband, Lee Milne. Today, he has been jailed for killing his wife in a landmark case

View 4 Images Kimberley Milne tragically jumped to her death following a campaign of abuse (Image: Daily Record)

Brave Kimberley Milne spent the last months of her life trying to free herself from her abusive husband's clutches, but each time he would claw his way back in to terrorise her.

‌



The 28-year-old, loved by friends and family, had a bright future ahead of her before her spark was cruelly stamped out by a man who coerced her into a marriage she never wanted. Soon after he pressured her to move in, the living nightmare began.

‌



Lee Milne, 40, spent 18 months tormenting his wife in a sick campaign of terror. The coercive control - a psychological form of abuse where a perpetrator erodes a victims' sense of self with manipulation, surveillance and humiliation - was unbearable for Kimberly, who already struggled with her mental health.

‌



Domestic abuser Lee Milne jailed for eight years after wife's tragic bridge jump READ MORE :

View 4 Images Lee Milne has been jailed for killing his 'terrified' wife Kimberly (Image: Facebook)

Milne controlled her finances, attempted to cut contact from loved ones and called her offensive names. It's a sickening tactic abusers use to reduce a victim to a shell of themselves in order to maintain their hold over them.

Isolated and vulnerable, Kimberley also suffered physical attacks and lived in constant fear of retaliation. She told the police that Milne spat on her and strangled her. He also punched her in the ribs while she begged him to stop.

‌



Eventually, the abuse became too much to bear. On 27 July 2023, Kimberley died after being struck by vehicles when she jumped from a motorway bridge on to the A90 in Dundee. Milne was convicted of killing her in the first case of its kind in Scotland. Today, he has been jailed for eight years. Here, we look at Kimberly's brave account of her devastating struggle before her death, and the agony of her final hours...

The insidious abuse

The court heard that on one occasion in 2022, Milne went through Kimberley's phone and lashed out. "Lee and I were in his home and he went through my phone," she told police. "He saw messages from other men before we were together. He got angry and started to shout and swear at me."

"Immediately after this he put both hands around my neck and pinned me against the kitchen wall. After a while he swapped his hands, pressed his right forearm against my neck. A few seconds passed and he let go and started crying, saying how sorry he was."

‌



In another incident, in late 2022, she told officers: "Lee repeatedly punched my ribs and I was begging him not to hurt me but he was not listening. I felt unsafe so I decided not to leave that night. I slept with a knife under my pillow as I was so frightened of him."

Police constable Owen McLaughlin, who spoke to Kimberley on 8 May 2023, also told the court that she told him Milne isolated her from friends and put her phone in water.

View 4 Images Lee Milne denied the charges but was found guilty in March (Image: Mike Gibbons)

‌



On one occasion in November 2022, Milne got angry when she asked to be taken home and struck her, causing her to fall and hit her head on a wall, knocking her unconscious.

On an occasion in May the following year, Milne seized her by the throat when she asked to be taken home, and choked her and shouted at her, causing her to run to another room and barricade herself in with a table. After forcing himself in he repeatedly punched and bit her, and threatened to hit her with a mirror that he then threw against a wall.

The court also heard that during another incident, Milne pulled Kimberley to the ground by her hair, later apologising and claiming he was "not that type of guy".

‌



Kimberley's brave account to police officers wasn't the only time she sought help. She also told a doctor that she was manipulated and tricked into marrying Milne, and had been dealing with domestic abuse for two years.

At trial, prosecutors read out medical notes February 2023, just five months before Kimberley's death. The record said: "Describes husband as manipulative and tried to make her feel she is losing her mind." Another noted that the abuse included "physical and mental" deterioration.

In another entry from May 2023, jurors heard that Kimberley "states [she] never believed in marriage ad [sic] feels tricked into agreeing to same. It also said: "Reporting husband as manipulative and a bully."

‌



Kimberley

In the hours leading up to his wife's death, Milne had acted in an aggressive and intimidating manner towards her. This included driving erratically when she was in a car with him, shouting and seizing hold of her, which put her in a significant state of fear, distress and alarm, the court heard.

A witness told the court that she saw a man and woman appearing to have an row outside on the night Kimberley died. Daisy White, 25, thought it was a "father-daughter situation" at first. The witness went shopping before spotting the pair again outside a flooring shop at the Kingsway Retail Park in Dundee.

The witness said this time the man was "trapping" the woman against the wall. Asked what the woman was doing, White told jurors: "Cowering, scared. She did not really do much. There was not much she could do. It did not look like [she was responding to the man] - she seemed too frightened."

‌



View 4 Images Kimberley lived in fear of her husband (Image: Daily Record)

White said she had been "concerned" for the woman and, asked why, she responded: "It was a man making a young woman scared. It is going to be alarm bells."

That evening, Kimberley died after being struck by a lorry when she took her own life by jumping onto the motorway.

‌



Kimberley's distraught mother, Lynne Bruce, told police how her daughter's killer woke her up the next morning, telling her that she had "gone". Bruce said she was told Kimberly had crashed Milne's car before he followed her on foot to a bridge.

In a statement read out in court, the 54-year-old is said to have explained: "I did not know what he was on about. He came in the house. He said something along the lines of Kim had pulled the steering wheel and crashed the car.

"He then said Kim had gone up to the bridge and he had chased her. He tried to grab her hands and she looked up at him, shook her head before jumping off. He then said he lay beside her."

‌



The mother said she was "devastated" when Milne told her what happened. Bruce also told jurors that her daughter had been acting "erratically" on the day of her death, and recalled seeing injuries on Kimberley that, she was told, Milne was responsible for.

Landmark sentencing

Milne had denied culpable homicide and a separate charge of domestic abuse but was found guilty at Glasgow's High Court in March. It's the first case of its kind in Scotland. In England there has only ever been one conviction, after stalker Nicholas Allen pleaded guilty to the manslaughter of his former partner Justene Reece in 2017.

Professor Jane Monkton Smith, an internationally renowned expert in homicide, coercive control and stalking, told the Mirror: "Coercive control usually either causes the mental health vulnerability or exacerbates it. We cannot separate the coercive control from the suicide. "It traps people in a situation where they cannot escape the person who is controlling them. And for some people, who try to escape, they can come to feel that there is no way out. This person is going to be abusing them for the rest of their life. They've tried the police, they've tried mental health help, they've tried domestic abuse services, they've tried going to their GP. Nothing gets rid of this person. And it's the entrapment."

‌



Reacting to today's sentencing, Jess Denniff, Head of SafeLives Scotland, also told us: "This is the first case of its kind in Scotland, and it should be a turning point. Kimberley Milne's death shows the devastating reality of coercive control. It is a sustained pattern of intimidation, isolation, degradation and fear that can utterly devastate someone's mental health. What Kimberly suffered was profound torment, and this case makes clear that abuse of this kind can be fatal.

"With the Scottish election approaching, there is a huge opportunity for the next Government to act. We need a step change in how coercive control is understood across policing, health, social care and the justice system, and in how suspected suicides after domestic abuse are recognised and investigated. This case must mark the moment Scotland stops underestimating the impact of coercive control, holds perpetrators to account, and makes sure survivors get the joined-up support they need sooner."

Meanwhile, following Milne's conviction, Detective Chief Inspector Craig Kelly said: "Our thoughts are with Kimberley's family and friends following this verdict. They have dealt with her tragic loss with great dignity and hopefully this outcome will provide a degree of closure.

‌



"Our investigation found that his behaviour in the time leading up to Kimberley's death was truly shocking and placed his partner in such fear that she took a course of action to get away from him which led to her death. She was very clearly terrified of him on that night. It is a tragedy that she lost her life as a consequence.

"Our investigation also uncovered a series of domestic offences against Kimberly over an extended period of time, exposing him as a cruel, manipulative and violent man.

"Our officers are determined to ensure women and girls live free from violence and abuse. We are relentless in our focus on tackling domestic abuse. It will not be tolerated, and perpetrators will be held accountable."

Article continues below

For confidential support, call the 24-hour National Domestic Abuse Freephone Helpline on 0808 2000 247 or visit womensaid.co.uk.

If you or your family have lost a friend or family member through fatal domestic abuse, AAFDA (Advocacy After Fatal Domestic Abuse) can offer specialist and expert support and advocacy. For more info visit www.aafda.org.uk

For mental health support, contact the Samaritans on 116 123, email them at jo@samaritans.org or visit samaritans.org to find your nearest branch.

News.title: Vladimir Putin chilling Telegram clampdown could signal 'endgame' in Ukraine war
News.content:
Vladimir Putin chilling Telegram clampdown could signal 'endgame' in Ukraine war

The Kremlin’s attempts to restrict the hugely popular Telegram app may signal looming 'unpopular decisions', the Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky has warned

View 2 Images Putin's Kremlin has clamped down on social media ahead of potential unpopular decisions, Zelensky warned (Image: AP)

Vladimir Putin could be preparing for either a dramatic escalation of the war or a potential endgame, Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky has warned.

‌



The Ukrainian president suggested the Kremlin’s clampdown on Russia’s main messenger Telegram could signal looming “unpopular decisions”. These may include military mobilisation reaching Russia’s biggest cities for the first time.

‌



Putin may be preparing for "people from Moscow and St Petersburg going to the front - and bringing back corpses," the Ukrainian leader said.

‌



Until now, the Kremlin has mainly recruited "cannon fodder" from poorer and more remote regions, often many time zones from Moscow. But new footage shows burgeoning graveyards in the sprawling region surrounding the capital.

Zelensky said the crackdown on Telegram - a key platform for both pro-war bloggers and independent voices in Russia - suggested the authorities were preparing to control public reaction to unpopular decisions with Soviet-style censorship.

Today the app faced severe restrictions and was barely working across Russia. "I think it’s to make unpopular decisions," he said.

‌



View 2 Images Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky (Image: IGOR TKACHENKO/EPA/Shutterstock)

NATO fighter jets scrambled as Russian spy plane spotted over Western defences READ MORE :

"Perhaps it’s the end of the war in one form or another. Or, on the contrary, an escalation of the war. Then it would mean even greater mobilisation for them."

He warned that either scenario would carry risks for the Kremlin, with Russian society divided between fanatical war supporters and those who would resist further escalation. According to Zelensky, around 20 to 25 per cent of Russians have been radicalised by propaganda and would oppose any settlement - while others could react negatively to deeper mobilisation.

‌



"Soon we will see which scenario Putin has chosen," he told journalists.

The outspoken Zelensky warning comes as he and Putin reached rare agreement to abide by a 32-hour truce starting on Saturday and covering Orthodox Easter Sunday this weekend. The warning comes as Zelensky said Russia is continuing to expand its forces inside Ukraine - even as Ukrainian troops inflict heavy losses.

"In a month, we destroy the same number of occupiers that they mobilise," he said - but added that Moscow is still increasing troop numbers by drawing on strategic reserves. He claimed this was a "risky step" for Russia, as it weakens its borders elsewhere.

‌



Zelensky also revealed that Ukrainian and British intelligence assessments dismiss Moscow’s latest battlefield ambitions as unrealistic. Russian commanders are aiming to seize Druzhkivka, Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk by the end of April, he said, based on leaked intelligence.

He declared: "This is impossible." British intelligence, he added, "does not see any possibilities" for Russia to achieve those goals within the timeframe, said Zelensky.

He forecast a crunch time for peace talks in the coming months, following major damage to Russian oil refineries and exporting ports by Ukrainian missiles and drones. A potential trilateral meeting with Russia, Ukraine and the US could take place as early by June if Russia chooses de-escalation - but cautioned that time is limited.

Article continues below

With the US expected to shift focus to domestic politics ahead of elections, he suggested August could act as a de facto deadline for serious negotiations. “This spring-summer period will be quite challenging politically and diplomatically,” he said.

Ukraine could face both battlefield pressure and diplomatic pressure he warned. But he insisted Kyiv understands its “national interests” and red lines.

News.title: 'I was dying in bed when I saw my dead grandmother who saved me – but she wasn't alone'
News.content:
'I was dying in bed when I saw my dead grandmother who saved me – but she wasn't alone'

A woman who went through a near-death experience after suffering a massive asthma attack has described meeting her late grandmother, and two other major biblical figures

View 4 Images Amber Baker's life was changed completely by her experience (Image: Jam Press/@malibumedium)

A woman who says she effectively “died” while suffering from an asthma attack has described how she had a vision of being restored to life by the spirit of her grandmother, who had passed away some years before.

‌



Amber Baker had suffered with asthma since childhood, but one particularly severe attack, brought on by a bronchial infection, left her hovering between life and death. Amber had already been treated in hospital, but had been sent home after being given a prescription for steroids, and was using a CPAP to help stabilise her breathing.

‌



Then, in the early hours of one morning in November 2018, Amber started having an asthma attack and wasn’t able to reach her phone to call for help. As her consciousness began to fade, her late grandmother Elaine appeared and came to her aid.

‌



She recalled: “I saw a white, hazy figure walk through my door and come to me, immediately laying her hands over my forehead. She began to calm me and breathe into my body and chest.

“My whole body started to go up and down and I felt as if my chest was opening with every breath more and more. I was completely taken over by her essence, given one breath after another, breathing open my chest and feeling peace and love.” But Amber also became aware of other presences around her.

View 4 Images Amber with Elaine (Image: Jam Press/@malibumedium)

‌



Amber says that a second sprit, named Mary, was working with her late grandmother to help her fight off the potentially-fatal asthma attack: “She was pure, unconditional love and didn’t say anything but felt like an anchor.”

Amber claims the two figures helped her to breathe for what felt like 30 minutes, and miraculously, she felt her chest expanding with every breath.

She said: “I was on my side and then my grandma’s spirit moved me to my back and my hands automatically went up as if to receive: She said ‘receive’ over and over again.

‌



"I felt another layer of opening and the tightness began to subside as my whole body was permeated by a rapture of love and deep breathing, opening my whole chest and torso. I asked her to please not stop until I could comfortably go to sleep.

“Knowing I was communicating directly with my grandma, she assured me she wouldn’t,” Amber added. “I was totally aware of what was happening, and completely astonished but grateful at the same time, knowing she was saving my life.”

View 4 Images Amber recovered from her astounding incident and is now a spiritualist (Image: Jam Press/@malibumedium)

‌



Incredibly, Amber then described seeing a third presence standing at the foot of her bed – whom she identified as the “gigantic” form of Archangel Michael.

She said: “His frequency filled the entire room and all of my awareness. He had a warm, orange, reddish glow.

“His features weren’t defined the way we see a person – he had the shape of a human form, but his body was fluid energy, moving like water, glowing with light.”

‌



It was at this point that Amber felt herself “leaving” her body and travelling down a “tunnel of light”, before the three beings shared a message with her. She explained: “They said that I am just a seed in the universe, a physical body that is not bound by my physical body but boundless to unlimited consciousness and power.

“As my mind expanded into this awareness my body felt smaller and farther away. I could feel myself tapping into an omnipresent, omniscient power and entering another level of consciousness. I knew I was meeting God."

View 4 Images Amber had been very close to her grandmother (Image: Jam Press/@malibumedium)

‌



This moment, Amber says, completely changed the course of her life: “Archangel Michael told me that my angels, Mother Mary and he, are always with me and that they would bestow upon me a miraculous healing to show me the power of this unlimited source that we can access at any time.”

The next thing she recalled was being in the “afterlife”, while her ‘guardian angels’ healed her body. She said: “I had crossed over but I was not dead.”

Amber says she was “reborn” back into her body, and felt “alive in a way I had never felt before”. She said: “I felt like a completely different person. I knew my divine presence had been activated."

Article continues below

Amber now works as a spiritual teacher and healer. While her experience might seem improbable, it chimes with near-death experiences reported by many thousands of people over the centuries. Individuals who have been close to death often report a sense of detachment from the body, feelings of peace and joy, passing through a tunnel, and encountering a bright “spiritual” light or, as in Amber’s case, deceased relatives

News.title: Drug dealer brought down after 'Turkey teeth' selfie led to arrest
News.content:
Drug dealer brought down after 'Turkey teeth' selfie led to arrest

Coran Davies sent the selfie from a dentist's chair showing off his new teeth, but he had no idea his friend's phone was being checked by police

View 2 Images The teeth picture that helped police pin Coran Davies (Image: South Wales Police)

A drug dealer sent his mate a selfie showing off his brand new "Turkey teeth" but unknowingly led the police to his arrest.

‌



Coran Davies pinged the image to his pal while sitting in the dentist's chair, proudly displaying his bright new teeth. More messages between the two however discussed supplying cocaine and cannabis - but Davies had no idea his friend's mobile was already being investigated by detectives.

‌



Officers deployed retrospective facial recognition technology on the photo, which led them straight to Davies. South Wales Police revealed that on an earlier date, officers had executed a search warrant under the Misuse of Drugs Act in Treherbert, Wales. Cops said they found an ounce of cocaine, cannabis and various drug paraphernalia.

‌



View 2 Images Davies (left) sent the picture to his mate Dale Howell (right) (Image: South Wales Police)

Months later, in March 2025, plain-clothed officers spotted Davies, 23, behind the wheel of a black Ford Fiesta travelling through Tonypandy, Rhondda, and arrested him, reports Wales Online.

‌



Dale Howell, 25, was also in the vehicle as a passenger and was likewise taken into custody. Both men, from Porth, were found to be carrying cocaine, cannabis and thousands of pounds in cash when searched.

The pair were jailed on Thursday, April 9, for supplying class A drugs and cannabis. They pleaded guilty to drug offences and acquiring criminal property — namely cash — and appeared before Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court. Davies was handed a 48-month prison sentence, while Howell received 36 months behind bars.

In a statement, South Wales Police said: "Two men from Rhondda were jailed on Thursday, April 9, for supplying class A drugs and cannabis. Coran Davies, 23, of Porth, was arrested after officers used retrospective facial recognition technology on an image he’d sent to his drug dealer friend’s phone.

Article continues below

"The image was of him on a dentist’s chair, having just had treatment for new teeth in Turkey and further messages referenced supplying cocaine and cannabis. Little did he know, his friend’s phone was already being analysed by detectives as part of an ongoing investigation."

News.content: The long-term consequences of the war will reverberate across the Middle East and beyond. A few weeks of Iranian attacks have done lasting damage to that strategy for modernisation and development. They are also reassessing their alliances with the US. News.title: How the cost of holidays, food and clothes is rising - despite the Iran ceasefire
News.content:
By-products from petrochemicals are used to produce drugs including painkillers, antibiotics and vaccines.



The UK imports most of its generic medicines, with 30% coming from India, which in turn depends on the Gulf to supply a significant proportion of its crude oil imports.



The UK was experiencing some product shortages before the war, and recently NHS leaders and pharmacies raised concerns about supplies and prices. Last week the government said it wasn’t aware of any supply issues caused by the conflict.



The National Pharmacy Association says the war has pushed up the cost of transporting and manufacturing some medicines.



Some pharmacies say they’ve increased the cost to customers of common generic over-the-counter medicines, such as paracetamol and hay fever treatments, by about a fifth.



The NPA says some wholesale prices for pharmacies ordering in stock have almost doubled since the start of the war, and it anticipates more of these extra costs will be passed on to patients in the coming weeks.



There won’t be a change to how much people pay for their prescriptions, it says, as these prices are fixed by the NHS.

News.title: Rory McIlroy's golf does the talking after busy Masters build-up
News.content:
Almost all the talk about Rory McIlroy in the build-up to this year's Masters related to the pomp.

In comparison, discussion about whether his game is there to secure a rare back-to-back Masters win felt somewhat neglected.

When last year's winner was finally able to focus on his golf on Thursday, McIlroy reminded everyone he is not in Augusta this week simply to serve up the Champions' Dinner.

He is here to play. And he is here to win.

The 36-year-old from Northern Ireland shares the first-round lead with American Sam Burns after carding a five-under par 67, ensuring anybody who was sleeping on his chances has been stirred.

McIlroy was among only 16 players in the 91-man field to finish under par, with conditions expected to get even firmer and faster over the next three days.

England's Justin Rose, who was agonisingly denied his first Green Jacket by McIlroy in a nerve-jangling play-off last year, is three shots behind the leaders and alongside world number one Scottie Scheffler on two under par.

"I think winning a Masters makes it easier to win your second one," said McIlroy, who is aiming to join Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods as the only men to retain the Masters.

"It's hard to say because there are still shots out there that you feel a little bit tight with, and you just have to stand up and commit to making a good swing and not worry about where it goes.

"But it's easier for me to make those swings and not worry about where it goes when I know that I can go to the champions' locker room and put on my Green Jacket."

Defence secretary John Healey has insisted the US remains “absolutely locked into” Nato, despite Donald Trump’s scathing criticism of the alliance.

The US president unleashed yet another social media rant criticising Nato on Wednesday evening, accusing them of not being “there when we needed them”.

His latest in a string of critical remarks about Nato came after he met with secretary general Mark Rutte, where the White House said Trump planned to have a “a very frank and candid” conversation about his frustrations with the alliance.

But speaking on Friday amid increasingly fractured relations between the UK and US, Mr Healey said it would be better to “focus on our actions” rather than Mr Trump’s social media posts.

Insisting the US remains committed to Nato, he said: “You know, if we focus on our actions, rather than just simply the exchange of words and social media posts, then the fundamentals for me remain that America is absolutely locked into - with benefits as well as massive contributions - to Nato.”

open image in gallery John Healey said it would be better to “focus on our actions” rather than Mr Trump’s social media posts. ( AP )

He told the London Defence Conference: “We have to do more – we are, and we will – on the European side. And there are, there are deep values that our nations share, that in the end, will see us through the ups and downs of the political cycles, as as they have done both sides of Atlantic in previous decades.”

Trump embarked on another online rant targeting the alliance on Wednesday evening following his meeting with the Nato general secretary.

"NATO WASN'T THERE WHEN WE NEEDED THEM, AND THEY WON'T BE THERE IF WE NEED THEM AGAIN. REMEMBER GREENLAND, THAT BIG, POORLY RUN, PIECE OF ICE!!!” he wrote on Truth Social.

At a White House briefing before the meeting, his press secretary told reporters that Mr Trump "has discussed" pulling out of Nato.

Speaking on Friday, Sir Keir Starmer said European allies need to do more in Nato after Mr Trump ramped up threats to leave the alliance.

“We’re very strong supporters of Nato and I’ve been making the argument for some considerable time that we need to do more,” he said.

open image in gallery Trump and Rutte in a White House meeting last year ( AP )

“It’s the single most effective military alliance the world has ever known. Do we Europeans need to do more? Yes, I’ve been making that argument for the best part of two years, to our European partners as much as anybody else. We continue to make that case and we will make that case.”

He added: “It is in America’s interests, it’s in European interests. Nato is a defensive alliance, which for decades has kept us much safer than we would otherwise have been.”

Strains on the alliance have been highlighted by the response to the US president’s war on Iran, which has prompted an economic shock felt around the globe.

The US president has previously raised the possibility of the US quitting Nato, branding it a “paper tiger”.

He has raised issue with the contributions paid in by fellow Nato members, arguing that the US has been carrying other countries financially.

Asked whether Mr Trump’s position represents a longer-term shift in the relationship, Mr Healey said on Friday: “I think this is a long term shift where Europe has to recognise that we've got to do more of the heavy lifting for our own security and within Nato.”

The relationship between Downing Street and the White House has come under particular pressure, following a barrage of scathing remarks made by the US president in response to the UK’s refusal to become involved in his offensive operations.

open image in gallery The relationship between Downing Street and the White House has come under particular pressure ( PA Archive )

In a recent jibe, Mr Trump likened Sir Keir to Neville Chamberlain at a White House Easter event on Monday, telling reporters the UK had “a long way to go”.

Sir Keir spoke to Mr Trump about the need for a “practical plan” to get shipping going through the Strait of Hormuz in the wake of the Middle East ceasefire on Thursday evening.

The call between the leaders came shortly after the prime minister criticised the US President over the knock-on effects of the Iran conflict, saying he was “fed up” with bills going up in the UK “because of the actions of Putin or Trump”.

News.title: Domestic abuser jailed for killing wife who took her own life after campaign of abuse
News.content:

A domestic abuser who was convicted of causing the death of his wife after she took her own life following an 18-month-long campaign of abuse has been jailed for eight years.

Lee Milne, 40, was found guilty of culpable homicide after his wife Kimberly Bruce or Milne, 28, fell from an overpass and was struck by a vehicle on the A90 Kingsway West on Thursday, 27 July, 2023.

Police said her death followed a “shocking” pattern of behaviour from Milne that left Ms Bruce “terrified”. In the hours before she died, Milne was found to have been driving erratically when she was in a car with him, shouting at her and seizing hold of her.

At a sentencing hearing on Friday, Milne was jailed for eight years, alongside a three-year extended sentence, meaning he will be on licence following his release. His conviction is believed to be the first of its kind in Scotland.

In a victim impact statement from her family, the court heard that Ms Bruce was “a much-loved daughter, sister, aunt, and they are devastated by her death.”

The judge said: “Nothing I can do or say can bring her back or ease their grief.”

Milne was also found guilty of a number of domestic abuse offences committed against Ms Bruce between January 2022 and July 2023. These included physically and verbally abusing her, coercing her to move in with him and marry him, attempting to cut off her contact with friends and family, and controlling her finances.

On one occasion in November 2022 Milne got angry when she asked to be taken home and struck her, causing her to fall and hit her head on a wall, knocking her unconscious.

On an occasion in May the following year, Milne seized her by the throat when she asked to be taken home, and choked her and shouted at her, causing her to run to another room and barricade herself in with a table.

After forcing himself in he repeatedly punched and bit her, and threatened to hit her with a mirror that he then threw against a wall.

CCTV footage from around the Kingsway area of Dundee on the day Ms Bruce died captured Milne’s aggressive behaviour towards his wife directly before her suicide.

Footage showed her cowering from Milne while he shouted at her, walking away as he drove at her, and hiding behind a wall and trailing slowly behind him as he led the way.

Following his conviction, Detective Chief Inspector Craig Kelly said: “Our thoughts are with Kimberly’s family and friends following this verdict. They have dealt with her tragic loss with great dignity and hopefully this outcome will provide a degree of closure.

“This was an extremely complex investigation and involved very close work with the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service to ensure that Lee Milne has been held accountable for causing the death of Kimberly.

“Our investigation found that his behaviour in the time leading up to Kimberly’s death was truly shocking and placed his partner in such fear that she took a course of action to get away from him which led to her death.

“She was very clearly terrified of him on that night. It is a tragedy that she lost her life as a consequence.

“Our investigation also uncovered a series of domestic offences against Kimberly over an extended period of time, exposing him as a cruel, manipulative and violent man.

“Our officers are determined to ensure women and girls live free from violence and abuse. We are relentless in our focus on tackling domestic abuse. It will not be tolerated, and perpetrators will be held accountable.”

Sir Keir Starmer has said his government must “remake our country” in order to ensure Britain is not “at the mercy of events abroad”, amid the economic fallout of war in the Middle East.

The prime minister is visiting Gulf allies this week as he seeks to join international efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran’s blockade of the key shipping route in retaliation to US strikes on Tehran has seen oil prices soar across the globe in recent weeks, sparking fears of its impact on the cost of living in the UK.

Writing in The Guardian, Sir Keir said the outbreak of war should serve as a warning for Britain to “build resilience” both at home and with European allies.

“Britain has been buffeted by crises for ​nearly two decades now,” he wrote, referring to the 2008 financial crash, austerity, Brexit, Covid, the war in Ukraine and Liz Truss’s disastrous mini budget.

open image in gallery Prime minister Sir Keir Starmer is visiting allies in the region ( Alastair Grant/PA )

“This time, it will be different. The war in Iran must now become a line in the sand, because how we emerge from this crisis will define all of us for a generation. And instead of hoping to return to the world of 2008, we will forge a new path for Britain – one that strengthens our energy, our defence and our economic security in a new age.”

He added that resilience has been “at the heart” of his approach to the war in order to avoid economic pressure on families in Britain.

“That is why, alongside our actions in the region, we’ve capped energy bills and invested heavily in the homegrown energy that can free us from the tyrants who manipulate gas prices,” he wrote.

“It is why, alongside staying out of the conflict, we’ve rebuilt our European alliances and boosted our defence capacity with the biggest sustained investment since the cold war.”

Sir Keir spoke to Donald Trump on Thursday night about the need for a “practical plan” to get shipping going through the Strait of Hormuz after a two-week conditional ceasefire was announced.

It came shortly after the prime minister criticised the US president over the knock-on effects of the Iran conflict, saying he was “fed up” with bills going up in the UK “because of the actions of Putin or Trump”.

open image in gallery Sir Keir Starmer and Donald Trump discussed the need for a ‘practical plan’ to reopen Strait of Hormuz ( PA Archive )

He told ITV’s Talking Politics podcast: “I’m fed up with the fact that families across the country see their bills go up and down on energy, businesses’ bills go up and down on energy because of the actions of Putin or Trump.”

Sir Keir will head back to the UK on Friday after visiting Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates this week to discuss efforts to reopen the strait.

He said the ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz must have “toll-free navigation” as part of the ceasefire amid reports Iran wants to charge for passage.

The ceasefire agreement, announced earlier this week, soon came under strain as Israel’s bombardment of Lebanon prompted Iran to close the shipping lane again amid disagreement over whether it was included in the ceasefire.

Asked whether he viewed the critical strait as now being open, Sir Keir said: “There are a lot of things being said – they need to be tested”.

He added that the UK’s position is that “open” means “open for safe navigation”.

“That means toll-free navigation and vessels can get through,” he told Talking Politics.

News.content:
